sections.title: Model overview and intended purpose
sections.text: Python Gradient Boosting (python-gradient-boosting) is a challenger model that is compared against the production default model; it informs but does not drive decisions. The business purpose shown here is inferred, and the model owner and intended business use or decision are not documented. It predicts the target default.payment.next.month using the UCI Default of Credit Card Clients dataset (30,000 records, 23 input variables), which is public demonstration data and not representative of a UK bank's current portfolio. The facts list the model as risk tier 2.

sections.title: Algorithm and methodology
sections.text: The model is a scikit-learn GradientBoostingClassifier with default hyperparameters and random_state set to the seed (default 42). The data is fetched from UCI dataset 350 and checked for 30,000 rows, 25 columns, no missing values and a default rate between 0.20 and 0.24. A stratified train/test split of 80/20 is then applied with random_state=42; the train fraction is inferred. The model uses 21 predictors: LIMIT_BAL, EDUCATION, MARRIAGE, the PAY, BILL_AMT and PAY_AMT series. ID, SEX and AGE are excluded, and no scaling or encoding is applied.

sections.title: Limitations and assumptions
sections.text: Performance, fairness, stability and monitoring metrics are computed only for the Statsmodels candidate; for this model only SHAP explainability is produced, using just the first 500 test rows. The decision threshold, hyperparameter rationale or tuning, model version, artifact hash, approval, deployment and monitoring status are not documented. The training data is historical Taiwanese data (April to September 2005), and deployment population representativeness and production calibration are unknown. The model assumes the library default hyperparameters are adequate and treats SEX and AGE as fairness-only attributes, and in demo mode it is trained on a synthetic dataset with only 3 predictors.
